box64-libs.source: archive.ubuntu.com (amd64, independent of the ARM64 guest distro)
box64-libs.description: x86_64 glibc runtime libraries for dynamically-linked x86_64 binaries under box64

box64-layer.description: Transparent Box64 execution layer: termdeb-wrap64 replaces each x86_64 ELF executable with an ARM64 launcher (termdeb-x86_64-launcher) that runs it through box64. Works for every exec path (execve, execvp, posix_spawn, JDK jspawnhelper) with no LD_PRELOAD, and never touches native ARM64 binaries or shared libraries (only ET_EXEC / PIE-with-interpreter ELFs are wrapped). termdeb-wrapd (continuous inotify watcher, host-side) keeps the layer up to date at runtime - AGP re-extracts x86_64 tools into fresh Gradle transform dirs mid-build, which a one-shot scan cannot see. Scan freshness uses a sidecar state file in the app's own data dir: the layer never writes stamps or other files into user/project directories, so tools that consume whole directories (aapt2 link, resource parsing) are never disturbed

systemd.source: deb.debian.org via apt inside the guest
systemd.description: Complete Debian userspace: termdeb-provision installs systemd, dbus, ca-certificates and locales on first start
systemd.mode: native (real chroot + systemd as PID 1) when the device has root (su) and the kernel exposes cgroups + PID namespaces; otherwise proot fallback with diagnostics

runtime-mode.description: termdeb-native (chroot/systemd launcher), termdeb-syscheck (kernel diagnostics), termdeb-provision (apt provisioning); merged /usr + full filesystem layout at install time
